comparison: Both strongly support the two-stage uptake mechanism with PG-dependence. OpenEval focuses on claims C3-C5, C26-C31 (kinetic data), C36 (stoichiometry), and C82-C84 (timescales). Peer review covers overlapping claims (C3-C5, C26-C31, C82-C84) plus additional claims about Ca2+ reversibility (C38-C39, C83) and lipid specificity (C32, C36-C37). Both evaluations are SUPPORTED with no disagreements.

Both support the high-affinity binding and 1:2 stoichiometry. OpenEval addresses C6, C59-C62 (fluorescence titration and dissociation constant). Peer review covers C6, C57-C62, C85 (including ITC validation). Both evaluations are SUPPORTED and align on the binding affinity measurements and stoichiometry determination.

Both strongly support complex formation in vitro and in bacterial cells. OpenEval and peer review address nearly identical claim sets (C7-C8, C63-C81) covering precipitate formation, characterization methods, and bacterial complex isolation. Peer review explicitly praises extension to bacterial membranes as a strength. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED with high agreement.

Both support reversibility of Ca2+-mediated binding. OpenEval focuses on C38-C43, C82-C83 (stopped-flow kinetics, Ca2+ sequestration reversibility). Peer review addresses C42-C51 (reversibility and irreversibility of different stages, conformational changes). Overlap on C42-C43. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED and agree on the reversible nature of initial Ca2+-mediated binding.

Both support irreversibility of PG-dependent insertion. OpenEval addresses C44-C51 (irreversible insertion, residual fluorescence, conformational changes). Peer review covers C42-C51 (reversibility vs irreversibility distinction, conformational changes). High overlap on C44-C51. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED and agree on the irreversible nature of membrane insertion.

Both support PG-specific binding versus other lipids. OpenEval addresses C32-C37 (no kinetic uptake with non-PG lipids, distinct binding modes). Peer review covers C33-C35, C40-C41 (different mechanisms with other negatively charged lipids, Ca2+-mediated recruitment). Partial overlap on C33-C35. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED.

Perfect match on claim set C52-C56 regarding weak G3P interaction. OpenEval explicitly supports the conclusion that weak G3P interaction cannot account for nanomolar DMPG binding. Peer review implicitly accepts these control experiments as part of 'solid in vitro evidence.' Both evaluations are SUPPORTED with complete agreement.

Both address conformational states but with different levels of certainty. OpenEval covers C88-C96 (CD spectroscopy data, conformational changes, decyl tail conformations) and rates as SUPPORTED. Peer review addresses C88-C101 (conformational changes and mechanistic model) but rates as UNCERTAIN, noting that 'discussion about conformational changes could be improved.' Disagreement on confidence level for mechanistic interpretations.

Both address the mechanistic model with uncertainty. OpenEval covers C98-C101 (pre-insertion complex, hidden tail, structural transition) rated as UNCERTAIN due to lack of direct validation. Peer review addresses C88-C101 (including mechanistic model) also rated as UNCERTAIN, noting mechanistic discussion needs improvement. Both agree the model is speculative and requires more support.

Both support connections to selectivity and resistance. OpenEval addresses C86-C87, C102-C107 (membrane composition differences, selective accumulation, threshold effects). Peer review covers C86-C87, C102-C105, C107-C111 (PG importance, selectivity, resistance mechanisms). High overlap on C86-C87, C102-C105, C107. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED, though peer review notes authors may 'overestimate their findings' regarding novelty.

Both support PG's dual role in binding and insertion. OpenEval addresses C108-C112 (dual role, connection to resistance mechanisms). Peer review covers C86-C87, C102-C111 (broader discussion of PG importance and resistance). Partial overlap on C108-C111. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED, with peer review noting the comprehensive analysis of PG's role.

Perfect match on claim set C113-C115 regarding PG-independent resistance mechanisms. OpenEval supports these literature-based observations as logically sound. Peer review does not specifically comment but implicitly accepts as part of overall manuscript acceptance. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED with agreement on acknowledging PG-independent resistance pathways.

Perfect match on claim set C97, C116 regarding speculative lipid II mechanism. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting this is 'purely speculative' with no experimental evidence. Peer review also rates as UNCERTAIN, with comments that authors 'overestimate their findings' and literature discussion 'could be improved.' Both agree this connection requires more support.

OpenEval addresses C1-C2, C9-C24 (background context and literature review establishing knowledge gap). No corresponding peer review evaluation found. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED but notes these are not novel findings, just contextual background from prior literature.

OpenEval addresses C25 (fluorescence property from prior work used as methodological foundation). No corresponding peer review evaluation found. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED but notes this is methodological detail from prior literature, not a novel finding.

OpenEval addresses C57-C58 (validation of 1:2 stoichiometry by fluorescence vs ITC). Peer review R2 covers broader binding affinity claims including C57-C58. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, viewing this as methodological validation. Peer review implicitly accepts as part of binding characterization. Both support the stoichiometry determination.

OpenEval R4 addresses C38-C43, C82-C83 (stopped-flow kinetics, Ca2+-mediated recruitment, reversibility). Peer review R1 covers broader two-stage mechanism including C38-C39, C82-C84. Partial overlap on C38-C39, C82-C83. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED and agree on the fast Ca2+-mediated binding phase.

OpenEval R4 addresses C38-C43, C82-C83 (stopped-flow kinetics, Ca2+-mediated mechanism). Peer review R8 covers C33-C35, C40-C41 (Ca2+-mediated recruitment, different mechanisms with other lipids). Minimal overlap on C40-C41. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED and agree on Ca2+-dependent binding capacity.

OpenEval R6 addresses C32-C37 (PG-specific kinetics and stoichiometry vs other lipids). Peer review R1 covers broader two-stage mechanism including C32, C36-C37. Partial overlap on C32, C36-C37. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED and agree on PG-specific linear relationship and distinct behavior from other lipids.
